text.p: Leading UK department store Harrods said on Wednesday its overall sales during the Christmas period rose by 10 percent compared with a year earlier and were two percent above its budget target.
"It was a very strong, very consistent Christmas," Michael Cole, Harrods director of public affairs told Reuters at the opening of the store's annual sale.
"For a retailer, it's a very encouraging picture. There's been no strong drop off in sales. It's been very consistent," Cole added.
On the Monday before Christmas, Harrods had sales of three million stg, compared with an average Harrods' daily intake of 1.2 to 1.5 million, he said.
"We've never done three million pounds on a Monday in the history of Harrods," he said.
Cole said the company had a particular pick-up in business gifts and luxury items during the pre-Christmas period, which runs from mid November to December 24.
